utterances.text: From the direction of Nedzarici, which is a neighbourhood that at the time was under the control of the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When you say "other side," who exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I mean the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now I'm just going to lastly ask you to mark the place where you lived and the Road of Death, as you have stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could we have the map 02872 brought up on the screen, please. Did I ask for this photograph to be tendered already?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admitted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I did. I'm grateful, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just waiting for the map, Witness, and then we're finished, at least I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could I please ask to have the 65 ter number of the map repeated.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And could I have the bottom left-hand part zoomed up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see Dobrinja there on the map, on your screen?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are you able to mark the location of the building that you lived in, firstly?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: That's my building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you put the letter A just beside that, please.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see on the map the Road of Death that you described earlier; and if you do, please mark it.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you mark that with the letter B, please.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And from that place, the Road of Death, can you, with the use of arrows, indicate the direction from which the sniper fire came from.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Sure. As far as this area. Later, the far end of this road became a little safer because it was behind the actual buildings, and that's why it became saver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This picture will become Exhibit P304, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that is the examination-in-chief. I'm grateful for the extra time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I represent Dragomir Milosevic. I'm Tapuskovic, attorney-at-law from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, Your Honours, it wasn't until a while ago that I noticed that this is really something I need to raise with the OTP. Mr. Sachdeva, how many statements did the injured party make?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you addressing -- who are you addressing?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's you that I'm addressing. I have two statements here provided by the witness; one dated the 10th of March, 1997; the other dated the 19th of May, 2006. The latest statement was amended by the previous statement, the earlier statement. It's only now that I have noticed. I have this one dated the 19th of May, 2006 and I have the one dated the 10th of March, 1997, and the witness, in his earlier statement, is making amendments to his later statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The procedure that we have here requires you to cross-examine the witness and not to address the Prosecutor. Any matters that you have must be cleared up in cross-examination. If that is not possible, then we will look at some other procedure. But we don't follow a practice where counsel address another counsel. It is for the witness to say how many statements he made, not Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all right, Your Honours. I was just trying to gain some time. But it's fine, all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you made two statements to the OTP, didn't you? One is dated the 10th of March, 1997 and the other, the 19th of April, 2006. Is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the statement dated the 19th of May, 2006, you make amendments there to some things that you said back in 1997. Is there any way you can possibly explain this, Witness? For example, the question about the first three months of the war, I was in the army, you say, in 1997, and then you amend this in the 19th of May, 2006 statement.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, simply because it was mistranslated at the time. I just happened to notice that. I wasn't in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm facing is a truly impossible situation. I have to use these two statements and I can't even explain this. I can start, but I really don't know what I'm supposed to do. I don't even know how I'm supposed to start. I have no idea. In 2006, he amends something that he said in 2007. I'm not sure how I should start this cross-examination. I don't think I'm able to, to be quite frank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's a matter for you, Mr. Tapuskovic. I can't understand why you're not able to cross-examine. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just see on the transcript, and also I heard in the translation, that counsel is saying that in 2006 he amends something he said in 2007, and I understand that counsel is saying that in 2006 he amends something that he said in 1997. Is that the -- I don't know if that's the source of confusion. But in any case, these are questions to be put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will just press on. I will just press on. This appears to be my own error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was it 2007 or 1997?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters confirm that counsel said 2007. The interpretation was accurate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was off the mark by about ten years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could have been worse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. My apologies. That can only be explained by my age and then, perhaps, excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll start with your first statement, sir, the 10th of March. Before that, however, I'd like to ask you a number of things about issues that were raised in chief. You said at the outset somewhere - and this is pages 32 and 33, line 24 of your evidence today - you said that the overhead lines sometimes broke down and there would be black outs because of the fighting along the front line, and then UNPROFOR would take you to those places; right?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It happened not only along the front lines, but the point was we couldn't go unescorted to those places to fix those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "because of the fighting along the front line," what exactly do you mean? Do you mean both of the warring parties firing at one another under given circumstances and then problems like these would arise?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I said. Most of the breakdowns happened on our side or along the front line itself. We didn't cause our own power lines to break down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mind you, you said because of the fighting along the front line. You made no distinction whatsoever as to what sort of fighting you were referring to. Firing by whom? Firing by both sides? Mutual firing or what? That's what I'm asking you. And I'm only asking you in relation to the time that General Milosevic spent in his position from the 10th of August, 1994 until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there when it happened. It was difficult for me to ascertain who was firing and where the firing was coming from. When we arrived, the firing had already been over, as a rule. It was peaceful enough for us to proceed with our job.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about the time we're talking about, especially summer of 1995? Was there not firing from both sides, by both warring parties? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, "firing from both sides"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I mean fire being opened at the same time by both the BH army and the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: There is no way I can know about the army, whether they were firing or not. I know where I was fired at from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm particularly interested in the 24th of May, 1995. I'm about to show you something that you said. But before I do that, can you please confirm that on the day in question there was a fierce of exchange of fire from both sides?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean by "fierce," "fierce firing"?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Also, fierce exchange of fire from both sides? Where in Sarajevo? Which part of the city. It's, in my view -- in my submission, the question is vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reformulate the question; make it more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, that's true. You're quite right and so is Mr. Sachdeva. But I'll come to that later. I'll need to return to that later, to keep myself from wasting any of my precious time and your precious time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking the witness this because, above all, there is one thing that I'm asking the witness: I'm not sure that I understand this correctly. The last time, or in the beginning, you said, didn't you, there were no offensive operations, no offensive was launched on that day, on the day in question.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Offensive operations by whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: How on earth could I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear on that day any firing, firing by weapons positioned in BH army-controlled territory in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I heard no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You heard no such thing. That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will need to show this witness a document. It's a BH army document in relation to that day. This document was signed by the commander of the 1st Corps, General Vahid Karavelic, about the firing from Sarajevo itself. This is DD00-0976. Can the document please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will read a single paragraph from this document. The first thing addressed here is operations by the aggressor along the whole front, the army of Republika Srpska, and then there is a paragraph that describes operations conducted on that day, the 24th of May, by the BH army from Sarajevo itself.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Am I supposed to read this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you could go to page 2. Page 2, paragraph 1. Page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I just ask if there is a translation available?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there a translation for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It has been submitted for translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just this first paragraph, all the way to the very end, please. Can you please read it outloud.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I can do it for you, if you like.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I prefer it if you did that for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. "All units within the 12th Division are at full combat-readiness. The units under attack by the aggressor throughout the day are successful in fighting. However, by the time this report was written, the aggressor had succeeded in temporarily taking trenches number 7 and 9. In order to win these trenches back, to take them back, fresh forces have been introduced and fighting is afoot. We returned the aggressor's fire with whatever artillery we had in terms of firing positions and in terms of preventing infantry attacks. Our present information indicates that in the course of fighting, one of our fighters was killed and five were slightly wounded in the 115 Mountain Brigade; four were slightly wounded by detonations in the 105 Mountain Brigade; one was seriously wounded and two were slightly wounded in the 1555 Mountain Brigade. No loss in terms of MTS, but the expenditure of ammunition was considerable." Therefore, according to this report, signed by Vahid Karavelic, the commander, there was firing throughout that day. Did you ever hear about this at all, or not?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I never heard about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This operation that lasted all day on the 24th of May, which is the date of this report, you say that you never heard anything in the place where you were on that day.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whose operations you're referring to. Listen, I'm not a military expert. The only thing I can tell you is what I experienced on that day, and that is the area surrounding the transformer station, the television building, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you took part in the operation but whether you heard this constant fire by the BH army from Sarajevo. Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, not from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness said that he didn't hear it, but I would kindly ask for this document to be marked for identification, because it's being compiled by the general who was in charge of this combat operation. There was shooting all day long; enormous quantities of ammunition and weapons were used on that day. Artillery was involved as well as were other weapons. The witness said no, but I believe that this deserves merit to be entered, because it refers to this specific date and that is the 24th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness said within the area of the transformer station - and again in answer to counsel's question - within the area of the transformer station and the TV tower, that he didn't hear any military activity. I am not fully versed with the area of responsibility of Division 12 or trenches 7 and 9, but there has to be some specificity as to the area which this fighting focuses on; otherwise, well, it's, in my submission, impossible for the witness to answer, which, indeed, he has done so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I thought you were going to address us on the question of whether it should be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I mean, I have -- the Prosecution has no objection to that. I don't, in my submission, submit that it should be entered into evidence. Of course, we are calling General Karavelic as a witness in this case and, in my submission, this would more appropriately be put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be marked for identification as Exhibit D95.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this point in time, I think it's my duty to tell you something. I made both a written and oral request to the Prosecution to submit to me, according to the rules, all the documents that they have relating to the operations carried out by the BH army. I haven't received any documents to this date. I know that everything has been scanned and that they have these documents available, but to this date they haven't complied with my request in supplying me with a single document. This document is one that I obtained myself, and I think it's my duty to draw your attention to this fact; that I still haven't received any of the documents that I requested both orally and in writing. However, this could be discussed on some other occasion. The only thing I would like to say is that this is an unfair practice. Now let me proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, if you hadn't said that, I think the Prosecutor would have let it lie. What do you want to say, Mr. Sachdeva?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, in response to that, all materials that are disclosable under Rule 66(B) and 68, it is my understanding, have been disclosed. Materials that relate to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and, in particular, to the 1st Corps that very have in-house have been disclosed. I'm not sure whether counsel is talking about materials that he obtained at the archives in Sarajevo, archives where we -- I mean, we went through the archives in Banja Luka and we received materials from those archives and they have been disclosed to the Defence. I don't know if he is talking about the archives in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But has the Prosecutor received the materials from -- has the Prosecutor received any materials from the archives in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Recently, not to my knowledge. And the ones that we have in-house have been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Tapuskovic, if you want to follow this up with a motion, then you may do so and be more specific. In the meantime, let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, let us not waste time. This can all be explained in writing. There is no need for us to dwell on it any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The place where this incident happened that you witnessed, how far is it from Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, you may put it like that, because we are talking about firing.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't tell you exactly. Mojmilo hill is not one point. Therefore, I cannot tell you how many metres it was from this place. There's a street that runs there as well. I cannot be precise. I can give you some figure off the top of my head, but that would not be an accurate one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it at the foot of Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it close to the foot of the hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Mojmilo is on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean immediately beyond the road?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How long is the ridge on Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. Whichever figure I tell you will not be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your profession and your fieldwork, when these pylons were knocked down, you went to repair them. Who was holding these positions on top of Mojmilo hill, along the whole ridge, at the time when you went to do this repair work?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I never went up there. This pylon was torn down a long time ago, connecting Lukavica, in 1990-something. I don't know. I never went up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go to fix overhead lines on Zuc mountain?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Whose positions were on Mount Zuc?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: It was a hill and part of it was held by our side and the other side was held by the other side. And the overhead line runs over the demarcation line between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbian positions were at the foot of the hill on the other side?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: There was several overhead lines; one was running from Vogosca and the other from Zreljevo. So one had to go across Vogosca and those hills. But I don't know who exactly was where. I didn't have time to look around. We had to do our job as quickly as possible and move away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I was not asking you about overhead lines. I asked you about the foot of Zuc hill. The Serbian positions were at the foot of this hill on the other side.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where their positions were. We never paid much attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But one could -- the BH army had full control over Sarajevo from Zuc.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you asking me to answer to that statement? I know nothing about military. I don't know who was in control of what. So, therefore, I cannot give you any answer. You should ask someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. From Zuc hill, did one have full visual control of Sarajevo by anyone standing on the top of this hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were lots of hills there. There was not only one hill. And who -- under whose control they were at that time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were lots of hills. There was Hum as well.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who was in control of those areas?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Listen, you're asking me too much about control and I can't tell you anything. These were military affairs. I really don't know. I was doing my job and that was all, and I was focussed on my job. I knew nothing about who was controlling which area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on now to the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown on the screen document DD00-957. That's the statement dated the 10th of March, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In that connection, I would like to ask you a few questions. First of all, is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: There is no statement. This is just details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There's your signature in the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to page 2. The first sentence in the second passage: "For the first three months of the war I was in the army." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, it's wrong. There was no army at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So that means that this is not true?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you had a work obligation because of your profession; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This work obligation, did that imply for certain purposes of the army, the needs of the army?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not what it meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, you say: "All the time I was involved in repairing power lines mainly between Zuc and Vogosca. I often had to work between the confrontation lines, when the lines were damaged during the fighting." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it's correct. It happened often, and mainly that's how it was, because the only power supply was coming from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So if there was fighting, you have to have two parties involved; is that correct, or not?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Probably so, but as I told you, I cannot tell you where fighting took place. We were just called to go out and we couldn't be able to say anything before we reached the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also say that it was the first time you ever heard about these air bombs, and then at the end of this passage you said: "I had a lot of experience with other ammunition."

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: That is also not correct. I don't know how it happened to be in my statement, whether it was due to mistranslation or whatever. I can only say that we had experience in hearing all kinds of projectiles. However, I wasn't a military expert in order to make this qualification. I was just speaking based on my personal experience. Even children knew these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So we may conclude that this is not true, what you said earlier?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: You're referring to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not an expert; therefore, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You went on to say: "I live in Dobrinja, and Dobrinja was fiercely shelled during the war." Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that the demarcation line ran through the midst of Dobrinja, because the front line ran through Dobrinja itself?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: There's still part of this line, because it -- in part, it coincided with the road. And this line still exists, not directly, but this part is under the control of the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: During the war, especially in the period that we are discussing here, was there exchange of fire in the town itself along the demarcation lines?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to Dobrinja or the town?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: My experience is that my flat was fired upon, but I can't tell you where these shots were coming. I would have to go out to the front line. And also, if it came from the other side, I wouldn't be able to say from which side it came.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Nedzarici and you said that shots were coming from Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You do know that Nedzarici was surrounded on all sides by Dobrinja and other parts of Sarajevo, like a ghetto, surrounded by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: You mean that it was surrounded?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have no time now to show this on a map. They were surrounded on all three sides. It was like a ghetto.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: If it's on just three sides, then they are not surrounded, are they, because there is always the fourth side, isn't there? They had a link to Ilidza and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but there was only this bottleneck that they could get through, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at Dobrinja where you lived, there were two entrances to the tunnel that ran under the airport at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever take that tunnel, given your job to repair the overhead lines at Igman?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: There are no overhead lines at Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about anywhere else outside Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: For the most part, we had organised missions. They were our escort. We would cross Ilidza on the way there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You never took that tunnel, then, did you?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In one paragraph further down the page, you say: "On the 24th of May, 1995 I was working at the transformer station, which was also our headquarters." All right, sir. You say "which was also our headquarters." Whose headquarters? Is this is word that is used in reference to anything that it not a military unit?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I just amended this sheet. I meant where we went to, where our work was, our headquarters. Everybody knows what "headquarters" means, although it could be taken to mean that, too. Headquarters. But it's not like headquarters; it's just, you know, like a place that we went to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: It can be used for sports, too, can't it?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course it can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But I'm putting it to you that this was a military headquarters and that it was a legitimate target.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: The transformer station? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the headquarters that was there.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No headquarters at all there. None at all. It was just a transformer station with people working there, not wearing uniforms or anything. We just had our kit, our tools, on us and that was that. That's absolutely out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What you're really saying is that it was misrecorded; you never said that, headquarters.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: That's just what I'm saying and that's why I drew everybody's attention to this statement. It says "headquarters." Headquarters can mean all sorts of things. You probably have in mind a military headquarters, but that is out of the question. I am positive about that. There was no such thing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm putting to you, Witness. That is where a military unit was headquartered that was in the area.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the next sentence, please, after this one about the headquarters. "On that day we were supposed to go to Vogosca, but we couldn't because of the fierce shelling in the area."

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: So what do you want to know about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Mr. Sachdeva wants to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's a minor clarification but I submit it's very important. In the English version of the statement, it says: "That day we were supposed to go to Vogosca. We did not go due to the heavy shelling in that area" and not "the area." Just so there's no confusion as to what area is being spoken about. I don't know if it's the same in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me just ask the interpreter to look at the text in B/C/S and tell us what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "In that area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: "In that area," yes. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of shelling are you talking about there, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: It's not me talking about it. There's a mission, an organised one, and then it's UNPROFOR that has to give the go-ahead. And then we're off and they say we can't go for this or that reason; it's not safe. And then we just don't go. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You make no reference to UNPROFOR. They weren't there at all.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: What exactly happened, I really can't -- their headquarters, that was the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that UNPROFOR was there the moment the air bomb landed?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's not what I'm saying. I'm talking about the missions that made our job possible, that secured our work somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Fine, then. "At about 10.00 in the morning, an air bomb flew over our heads and fell somewhere." That's what it says; right?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just after the shelling.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I think I amended that, too. There was no way I could have known at the time that this was an air bomb. I said it was something; I didn't say it was an air bomb. There is no way I could have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute, wait a minute. I'm quoting you. "Around 10.00 a.m. an air bomb flew over us." I'm asking you: Before it flew over you, you had never seen the air bomb, had you?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know where the bomb had come in from, do you?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. It came from the same direction, but I was inside a building; therefore, I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about this other one? You say that it flew over Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of, or something to that effect. It was by the sounds that we -- and we were watching. We were outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say, therefore, that you didn't see that one either? You just heard -- felt the sound.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. It was like the sound of an aeroplane, and we tried to see what it was and then it came closer. It got dark. There was this flash before our eyes nearly as it reached us. And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't understand the final part of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DD00-0957, Your Honours, can this please be admitted as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't understand the last part of the witness's answer. So I'm going to ask you to repeat it, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please speak one at a time to ensure an accurate interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters want you to speak one at a time. The sentence that we are concerned with, Witness, I'll just read it to you. You said: "It got dark. There was the flash before our eyes nearly as it reached us. And ..." That's where the interpreters lost you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember what I said, can I? That's it. That sounds very much like it. If the gentleman can perhaps repeat the question, I have no problem answering the same question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The essence of my question --

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: The other shell; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could the speakers please be asked again to speak one at a time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I need to ask you again: You have overlapping. It's a lack of discipline, a lack of rigour. Speak one at a time. Ask the question -- repeat the question, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other air bomb, he only heard the sound. He can't tell us where it came from, can he?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the bomb came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The bomb came from the direction of Mojmilo. That is precisely because we heard it, we watched it, and something dark hit that place and then there was this flash. And by that time I was on the ground. We were standing, the two of us, watching in that direction. Well, you can't ... can you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And how are you able to say that the bomb came from the direction of Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because we were standing. At first we thought it was an aeroplane, and I thought that, too. So we looked around to see the direction from which this plane was moving. However, it proved to be no plane at all. We looked, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On that note, we'll stop and take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there was a lot of confusion before the break and I need to go back to my last question. The 10th of March, 1997 statement that we have in front of us, page 2, I would like to read that back to the witness and then I expect him to answer. It's about this other bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you explained about the first bomb. And then if you could please look - it's halfway down the page - I will read slowly to you all of it. "The second bomb that injured me arrived after 2.00 p.m. I heard this one also coming from the same direction. My foreman, a colleague, and I left the building at that moment because I want to go home. Because it was quiet at the moment, we left. As soon as I left the gate with my colleague, I heard the sound of what I thought was a plane. It made the same sound. We heard it because we were already going uphill. We stopped, because we couldn't see the plane. Then we saw something black falling in front of us." So my question: You heard the sound, I'm putting to you that you heard a sound, as you explain here, but you saw nothing, and you only saw something once something black landed in front of you. Is that how it was, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we saw something land in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But prior to that, you had seen nothing at all, except for hearing that sound which, to you, was reminiscent of the sort of a sound that the plane makes; right?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that was before that and we thought it was a plane. The sound was coming closer and we just looked in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on this, however, this thing you saw flying through the area and made the sound that you heard, you didn't actually see it before it landed in front of you, did you?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can DD00-0957 be admitted as a Defence exhibit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statement will become Exhibit D96.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just one thing, Witness. Can you answer this: You said "up the hill." Where exactly did you mean?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a road going up past the transformer station from the TV building. It forks off; one goes to Svrakino Selo and the other the road goes towards Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Alipasino Polje is a valley; right? It's something that you said. You went up.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but Alipasino Polje is not all in the valley. There is a part of Alipasino Polje that is actually up a slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to be as brief as possible with the second statement. DD00-0965, the 19th of May, 2006. It's the one that I got mixed up a while ago. If that document could please be brought up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature here?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can move on to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 contains what we already discussed. "First, I was never in the army at the start of the war in 1992," and we clarified that. Then you went on to say as follows: "I only joined the other civilians from my apartment block to guard the building from attackers or any possible looters and vandals." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that you wanted to prevent attacks by looters and vandals, does that mean from looters and vandals within Sarajevo, in Dobrinja specifically?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We organised ourselves. Each entrance set up their own organisation, because that was the very beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. At the time when Dragomir Milosevic was the commander of the Sarajevo Corps, was the situation the same?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. Are you referring to the year 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no. No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who were those groups committing these acts inside Sarajevo at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know if they existed at all, at least not in my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any killings? Did people go missing? Were people taken from their homes, irrespective of whether they were Serbs, Muslims or Croats?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll skip paragraph 2 and move to paragraph 3. It refers to the bombs, and let's finally find out the truth. It says here: "Third, my statement says that at 10.00 a.m. I saw a modified air bomb fly from Lukavica." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. And then the following sentence: "I actually don't know where it originated from." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, because I didn't know where it was fired from. I'm not a military expert. I just could see the direction where it came from, but where it originated at, I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you one more thing and then I'll finish. You go on to say as follows: "This sentence" -- this refers to the direction from which the air bomb came -- "should be referring to the 2.00 p.m. air bomb which injured me."

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: That is why, because I was referring to the first bomb. I don't know about the first bomb. I was inside the building and it flew over the building. Therefore, I cannot say where it had come from. I can only guess by its sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But look here at the last sentence of this paragraph: "I cannot say where that 2.00 p.m. bomb originated. I saw it flying from the direction of Mojmilo hill, but I don't know how far on the other side of Mojmilo it came." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I don't know the exact location where it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In your first statement given in 1997, you said that you had heard a sound, and only after this black thing landed in front of you, you were able to see what it was.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you understand? We were listening to the sound first and then we saw this black object falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Before that you never saw anything in the air.

utterances.speaker: ENES JASAREVIC
utterances.text: You cannot follow a flight just according to a sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That concludes your evidence, and we thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, DD00-0957, which is a statement given on the 10th of March, 1997 -- oh, I apologise, Your Honours. DD00-0965, dated the 19th of May, 2006, I would like this to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I understand the next witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness is a protected through voice, face and pseudonym, and Mr. Cannata will be taking the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I'm told that we have to have a break to allow some technical matters to be attended to. How long?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ten, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Just to finish a document that was marked for identification with the previous witness - that was Luinovic - we have already received a draft translation and we have e-mailed that to the Defence. This concerns D94. So we don't have any more objection to have it tendered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we can admit that now as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can I also just ask that the last document tendered will be given Exhibit number D97. --- Break taken at 6.13 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours. Before we start, let me remind everybody in this courtroom that the witness is a protected witness. He has a pseudonym, which is W-12, and image and voice distortion. And to comply with these protections, we will ask the court officer to show the witness the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, can you be so kind to take a look at the document which is being shown to you now and confirm that the information contained therein is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I tender the pseudonym sheet into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P305, under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this witness is a 92 ter witness, so the Prosecution will seek to admit the witness statement, both statements. So I will ask the court officer to call up 65 ter number 2971, and please, not to be broadcast because of the protections granted to the witness. Can we have also the B/C/S version of the same document. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see your signature at the bottom of the first page of the English version?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to page 2 of both the English and B/C/S. Next page. Can we zoom a little bit, the B/C/S one. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this document as the statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in November 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you have reviewed this statement during our proofing session yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, do you confirm that that statement is true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And you also confirm that you would give the same answers if asked the same questions today, again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I tender this statement into evidence, under seal, with your leave, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be Exhibit P306, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to exhibit -- 65 ter 2972. Can we also have the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, again the same question: Do you see your signature at the bottom of page 1 of the English statement, the one on your left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we move to page 2, next page, in both the statements? Can we -- let me ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember that this is the statement that you reviewed in my office -- in an investigator's office yesterday in our proofing session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Is there any correction that you want to make to this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we zoom the B/C/S page, at the bottom, the last paragraph, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to make a correction on the right-hand side in the last paragraph where it says: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. With this correction, would this statement be true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes. So, there were female neighbours; one of them got killed and the other was injured but survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: The so corrected statement will be reflecting the same answer that you would give today if asked the same question again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I tender this statement into evidence, under seal, again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will become Exhibit P307, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have Exhibit P104, which is the map. So it will take a little bit to be loaded. Meanwhile, I will ask the witness a few questions, with your leave, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, were you a soldier with the ABiH between August 1994 and December 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you remember the corps and brigade you belonged to at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I was a member of the 1st Corps, 115th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: What rank, if any, or what kind of role did you have in the 115th Brigade between August 1994 and December 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: I didn't have a rank. I was a private on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I see that the map is now on the screen. Witness, do you see the map on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can we have zoomed the top right-hand corner. Just further down, please. No. That's fine. Okay, that should be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, the day -- at the time of the shelling incident, you stated that you heard a sound of a shell when you were on your way to the front line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the area of Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Very well. Would you be able to mark, with the electronic pen that Mr. Usher will kindly provide you with, the area that you just indicated on the map. And if you need it to be zoomed, just tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, this is where Brajkovac is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you put a small A, a letter A, within that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: You described that sound as -- well, let's put it this way: What was the sound you heard that day like? Was it the sound of a mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: No, it wasn't a sound of a mortar shell. I think it was a gun, a cannon or some heavier weapon, a gun or something like that. So it was -- it was a powerful sound, much more powerful than the one made by a mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And how did you make such an assumption? How did you establish, in your opinion, that it was not a mortar shell but, rather, a cannon shell or a different shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Well, a mortar shell produces a lower noise when fired. This was a loud noise, a loud shout, compared to a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you have any experience with mortar shells, any direct experience with mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: No, I don't, apart from the experience in the war that I acquired.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: So it would be fair to state that you experienced mortar shells in your capacity as a front line soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, but only based on the shells that were falling around me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: So, another way to put it: You heard mortar shells falling -- you heard the sound that a mortar shell makes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And that sound was different from the one you heard that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Very well. Did you see where these shells landed? Where did it impact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: No, I didn't. The weather was bad. But we assessed that it was the old part or the old quarter of Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you mark this -- this quarter on the map in front of you, as you did with the circle. Can you circle that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you put a letter B within the circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: How did you establish, how did you make the assumption, that the shell landed -- could have landed in the area that you just indicated in the map? On which basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Given that at the time I was living in Bistrik, which is the old part of the city, and I was quite familiar with Bascarsija, I knew that that is where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: We'll get back here to this point a little bit later. So let me ask you now: Did you see where the shell was fired from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: No, I didn't. But I heard the sound of it being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Would you be able to locate on the map the location which corresponds to the direction of the sound you heard that day? In other words, what you think is the place where the shell was fired. Can you mark it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It's the Vidikovac area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can you put a letter C within the circle you have just marked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you establish -- I mean, based on your knowledge and experience, how did you reach the conclusion that the shell you heard was fired from Vidikovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Well, because our positions were much lower. The highest position was at Colina Kapa, and the sound of its being fired was coming from the left and from a higher elevation, that is to say, from the direction of Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: So based on what you heard and what you observed that day, you were able to reach the conclusion that the shell was fired from Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Isn't Vidikovac a part of Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Let me go back to the question I asked you before. How did you establish that, since you didn't see the shell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't want to get up earlier, but I think that the witness cannot be asked whether it came from Mount Trebevic. Rather, he should be asked, where was the shot fired from, not whether it was fired from Mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm trying follow the line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist, I don't believe I said that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We had the question: "So based on what you heard and what you observed that day, you were able to reach the conclusion that the shell was fired from Vidikovac." But prior to that, the witness had said: "The highest position was at" so and so, "and the sound of its being fired was coming from the left and from the higher elevation, that is to say, from the direction of Vidikovac." So the witness had said that before. That's not leading, Mr. Tapuskovic. It was already in evidence. It can't be leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Honours, towards the end, that's what I heard, at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, the witness had already given the evidence that he heard the shot come from the direction of Vidikovac. He is merely repeating himself -- counsel is merely repeating what the witness said before. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Carry on. So, Witness -- let me check where we were when we stopped. Witness, I'm going ask you: How did you establish then, if you didn't see the shell landing, how did you establish -- how did you reach your conclusion that the shell landed in - and forgive my pronunciation - Bascarsija, the location indicated with the letter B on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Well, as I said before, I lived in that neighbourhood, the old town, part of Bistrik, and I know Bascarsija very well. From Brajkovac you can hear everything and you can see Bascarsija very clearly when the weather is fine. And it was because of that that we were able to establish that the shell landed in a part of Bascarsija, which is the old town.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: What was the weather like that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: It was quite bad. It was a foggy morning at about 8.00 or 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: You mentioned previously in your evidence that you reached the conclusion that the shell was fired from Vidikovac, because it's in a higher position with respect to which location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: In relation to Colina Kapa. Colina Kapa is much lower. It's at a level with Brajkovac. A bit higher up, perhaps, but for the most part, that would be it. Vidikovac is, again, higher up, and it was from that direction that we heard the echo of the shell being fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Can I ask you, you stated that you were part of the 115th Brigade. Do you stand by this evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Would you be able to mark on this map with a line the area of responsibility of the 115th Brigade that you belonged to, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes. The area of responsibility of the 115th Brigade was here, stretching from Kozija Cuka - I can only see Jarcedoli here - from the Miljacka river, and then all the way as -- this is where the Miljacka river is. And then Jarcedoli and then Dolovi and then Mala Colina Kapa, Velika Colina Kapa, Bogusevac, Brajkovac, Debelo Brdo, Vranjaca, and then from here down towards Debelo Brdo and Kovacici, down towards Grbavica and past the Jewish cemetery, around about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you be so kind as to put the number 115 and the letter B either at the -- let's say at the very bottom of your right, and corresponds with the "most" on the river. So to have on the record that the line describes the 115th Brigade line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: On the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: 115. Should I add anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And, please, the letter B.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I have very few -- a couple of questions and then I will be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: You are finished with this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: I have just one question for the witness. [Interpretation] Sir, you said that you were in Brajkovac and you heard detonations from Vidikovac. You said that you believed that the shells fell on Bascarsija. Now, my question is as follows: Did you see the shells pass by, those tracing bullets or bombs - I don't know how to call them - or do you only think that the detonations took place at Bascarsija, or that what you heard in Bascarsija was the result -- that that sound was the result of what happened on Vidikovac? In other words, is it possible that the detonations that you heard in Bascarsija came from elsewhere? What allows you to be so certain about what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly after the sound of the shell being fired, one could hear a detonation at Carsija, very soon after, and that's why we concluded that the shell had been fired from Vidikovac and had landed in the general Carsija area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it was not possible to see them like it was the case for the modified air bombs, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I couldn't see the Carsija area at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: May I carry on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Witness, how long did you serve with the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: From June 1992 to around about April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And you were -- you've been always attached to the 115th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: So the red line on the map which describes the area of responsibility of the 115th Brigade is your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Do you know what a 120-millimetre mortar is? Have you ever seen one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: Yes. I saw one back in the JNA, when I did my term with the JNA, back in 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: And in your experience as a soldier with the 115th Brigade and as an ABiH soldier, have you ever seen a 120-millimetre mortar within your area of responsibility, which is the area of the 115th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-12
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: That concludes my examination-in-chief, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I was forgetting to tender into evidence the map, as marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we will admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P308, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll have the cross-examination tomorrow. We'll break now until tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 2nd day of March, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
